description.value: An fMRI study examining smoking-cue-related brain activation in adolescent light smokers and nonsmokers.

spans.text: This study focused on adolescent light smokers to identify brain regions important during the developing stages of addiction.

description.value: Observational cross-sectional comparison of adolescent light smokers and nonsmokers, with participants undergoing fMRI during smoking-related and neutral cue blocks.

spans.text: Using fMRI, we examined whether adolescents with low levels of nicotine exposure (light smokers) display neural activation after exposure to smoking cues.

value: In smokers, significant activation from smoking versus neutral cues was found within the left and right frontal medial orbital regions, as well as the left amygdala, left anterior cingulate, bilateral posterior cingulate, right hippocampus, and right inferior and middle temporal regions. There were no significant activations in the nonsmoker control group.

spans.text: In smokers, we found significant activation from smoking versus neutral cues within both the left and right frontal medial orbital regions ( t = 5.09, p < .01 and t = 3.94, p = .01, respectively; , nonsignificant ROIs not listed). We also found significant activation in the left amygdala ( t = 2.26, p = .05), left anterior cingulate ( t = 2.47, p = .04), left and right posterior cingulate ( t = 3.27, p = .03 and t = 2.75, p = .03, respectively), right hippocampus ( t = 2.61, p = .03), and right inferior and middle temporal ( t = 2.80, p = .03 and t = 3.01, p = .03, respectively).
fMRI scans were obtained using an echo-planar pulse sequence

Next, fMRI scans were obtained using an echo-planar pulse sequence with T2-weighted images sensitive to blood-oxygenation-level-dependent contrast (time to repeat = 2 seconds; time to echo = 40 ms; flip angle = 90, matrix = 64 × 64, field of view = 40 × 40 cm 2 , 33 slices, 3-mm thickness).
